title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 57 (Punishment for Personation of Shareholder)

content.overview: Section 57 punishes any person who deceitfully personates an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to such owner. Liability includes imprisonment and fine.
content.glance: Deceitful personation of a security owner to obtain securities, warrants, coupons or money due — imprisonment and fine.
content.study: If any person deceitfully personates an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, and thereby obtains or attempts to obtain any such security or interest or any such share warrant or coupon, or receives or attempts to receive any money due to any such owner, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees. Current-law framing: prove deceitful personation of the owner; obtaining or attempting to obtain the security/interest/warrant/coupon or money due; apply the statutory punishment range.

sections.heading: Prohibited Conduct
sections.body: Deceitfully personating an owner of any security or interest in a company, or of any share warrant or coupon.

sections.heading: Object
sections.body: Obtaining or attempting to obtain the security, interest, warrant or coupon, or receiving or attempting to receive money due to the owner.

sections.heading: Punishment
sections.body: Imprisonment not less than one year and up to three years, and fine not less than one lakh and up to five lakh rupees.

examples.title: Personation to obtain shares
examples.body: A person pretends to be a registered shareholder and induces the company to issue a duplicate certificate or pay dividend. Section 57 is engaged.

examples.title: Attempt
examples.body: An attempt to obtain money due to a shareholder by deceitful personation is itself punishable under s. 57.

hypotheticals.question: Is attempt enough under s. 57?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The section covers obtaining or attempting to obtain the security/interest/warrant/coupon, and receiving or attempting to receive money due.

distinctions.title: Personation of shareholder (s. 57) vs personation for acquisition of securities (s. 38)
distinctions.left: Personating an existing owner to obtain securities or money due
distinctions.right: Fictitious-name applications and multiple applications for allotment

rows.right: Identity fraud in applications for new securities

misconceptions.trap: Only successful obtaining of shares is punishable.
misconceptions.correction: Section 57 also punishes attempts to obtain securities or money due by personation.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 57 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Prove deceitful personation of the owner. II. Prove obtain/attempt regarding security or money. III. Apply punishment range. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Personation facts; object of fraud; attempt or success; precise relief.

examTips: Quote the imprisonment and fine range.
